title: Chicago Engineer Niranjan Shah Named Distinguished Alumnus on Patel Anniversary
excerpt: The Sardar Patel University alumni community is honouring the Globetrotters Engineering co-founder for five decades of engineering and civic work in the United States, according to a November 2 announcement.
body:
• Sardar Patel University's alumni community has named Chicago engineer Niranjan S. Shah a Distinguished Alumnus as India marks the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, according to an announcement dated November 2, 2026.
  • Shah grew up in Pratapnagar in Gujarat's Narmada district, graduated from Birla Vishvakarma Mahavidyalaya in 1967, and co-founded Globetrotters Engineering Corporation in Chicago in 1974.
  • His firm's work includes Chicago's Deep Tunnel project, which received the American Society of Civil Engineers' Outstanding Civil Engineering Achievement Award, the announcement said.
  • The announcement said the honour drew a letter from President Biden and proclamations from Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson.

Niranjan S. Shah, a Gujarat-born engineer who has spent more than five decades building infrastructure in the United States, is being honoured as a Distinguished Alumnus by the Sardar Patel University alumni community, according to an announcement issued from Vallabh Vidyanagar, Gujarat, on November 2, 2026. The honour is tied to the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the university's namesake.

From rural Gujarat to Chicago

Shah grew up in Pratapnagar, in Gujarat's Narmada district, in modest circumstances, and graduated from Birla Vishvakarma Mahavidyalaya in 1967, according to the announcement. After moving to the United States, he made Chicago his home and in 1974 co-founded Globetrotters Engineering Corporation, the firm he is best known for.

The firm's projects, as listed in the announcement, include Chicago's Deep Tunnel flood-control system, Navy Pier, McCormick Place, John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital and O'Hare International Airport. The Deep Tunnel work received national recognition through the American Society of Civil Engineers' Outstanding Civil Engineering Achievement Award.

Public service alongside engineering

The announcement also records a Senate-confirmed presidential appointment for Shah to the board of trustees of the Barry Goldwater Scholarship and Excellence in Education Foundation, the federal programme that supports students pursuing research careers in science, engineering and mathematics.

Recognition in the United States

According to the announcement, the occasion received recognition from United States leaders: a letter from President Biden honouring Shah and commemorating Sardar Patel's legacy, a proclamation from Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias recognising the 151st birth anniversary and Shah's legacy, and a proclamation from Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson recognising Shah's contributions to Chicago and the bonds between the city and India. For the Gujarati diaspora in the Midwest, the honour links two stories at once: Patel's, whose birth anniversary India marks each year, and that of an engineer who left a Gujarat village in the 1960s and spent his career on the tunnels, hospitals and airport terminals of Chicago.
